Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: request to move up dedicated tranche for Aurora launch

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. We're going live with our consumer launch the week of May 17 and need the second dedicated tranche moved up by three weeks to avoid throttling at peak. Current committed start is June 7 under DEAL-3492. Can Redwood accelerate the tranche to May 24? Our ops team has indicated a hard dependency on the 4x A100 equivalent capacity to keep 99th % latency within SLA for our real-time features.

I'm attaching the Aurora capacity request PDF with traffic curves and a proposed phasing. If we can accelerate, we'll sign the SLA amendment and accept a short-term premium for burst capacity. If not, we need to discuss a soft cutover plan.

Tom
Tom Ellis

Tom —

Appreciate the heads up and the traffic curves. I'm looping in Ben (capacity ops) and Laura (sales lead for the account) as well as Monica from CS so we can converge quickly. Ben — can you surface potential options and the technical trade-offs (preemptible burst, split-commit, or quantized instance alternatives)? We need a recommendation by EOD so I can get back to Tom with an executable plan (and proposed SLA amendment language).

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-04-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: request to move up dedicated tranche for Aurora launch

Team —

Quick operational summary and options (see attached allocation_matrix_v2.xlsx):

1) Phase-forward (preferred): move Aurora's committed tranche to May 24 by reallocating 25% of idle reserve capacity and enabling a 10-day cross-customer burst window. Impact to Lumos: will delay their non-critical jobs by 7 business days; latency SLOs for Lumos' critical endpoints remain protected via routing.

2) Split-commit: carve the tranche into 60/40 split across May 24 and June 7. Aurora gets immediate baseline capacity; Lumos keeps majority of the original slot. This reduces risk of SLA breach but requires engineering to shard model placements (estimated 2-day change).

3) Quantization/worker substitution (contingency): offer a quantified pricing for running Aurora on 8-bit quantized versions of the same model on earlier hardware. Lower latency predictability but faster capacity fit.

Risk note: If both customers insist on full contiguous capacity, we hit a hard constraint requiring contractual tradeoffs (credits or premium incremental hardware).

Recommendation: execute option 2 (split-commit) + 10-day burst for Aurora, and offer Lumos a 15% invoice credit for sensitive peak days to compensate for scheduling shift. I attached the allocation matrix and a quick sensitivity table.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity & Entitlements, Redwood Inference
attachments: allocation_matrix_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 320KB)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Urgent: request to move up dedicated tranche for Aurora launch

Folks —

Thoughts from a commercial / renewal perspective: Aurora is in heavy PLG motion and accelerating their launch materially increases their ARR cadence; keeping Aurora running at the requested start yields higher ACV upside and reduces churn risk. Lumos is strategic but has a longer legal procurement runway and is willing to accept a phased start if it comes with a documented credit and explicit fallbacks.

Proposal: Accept Ben's recommended split-commit + 10-day burst for Aurora. Offer Lumos a formal credit (15% on three peak days) and a guaranteed start no later than June 7, with a technical playbook that preserves their critical endpoints. We'll convert the agreement into a declarative amendment and get countersigned.

Action items:
- Ben: update allocation_matrix_v2 with the split and flagged nodes by 4pm PT.
- Rishi: propose amendment language for Aurora (short premium for burst) and Lumos credit term.
- Monica: align with Lumos PO and confirm they accept phased start.

I'll take point on the commercial memo to leadership if needed.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
